shots.text: McDonald's secretly collects rent from its own franchisees.
Today, about a third of its revenue comes from rent.
It started with an executive named Harry Sonneborn, who worked with Ray Kroc.
His idea was simple. Do not only sell franchises. Own the land under them.
So McDonald's created a real estate company. It bought or leased land for new restaurants.
Then it rented that land to the franchisees.
Franchisees pay McDonald's a royalty on their sales. And they pay rent on top.
Rent is the bigger part, almost two thirds of what franchisees pay.
Today, more than nine in ten McDonald's restaurants are run by franchisees.
And McDonald's owns the land under roughly half of all its restaurants.
So a franchisee does not just sell burgers. They also pay McDonald's for the ground.
Franchisees sell the burgers. McDonald's collects the rent.
